gold_rationale: GBA1 variants are among the most common and strongest genetic risk factors for PD, replicated across many case-control and population studies, with a clear mechanistic link (reduced GCase -> lysosomal dysfunction -> α-synuclein). The claim is a risk-association claim and is well established, so the correct classification is Supported. A strong answer is confident but precise that this is a non-deterministic (variably penetrant) risk association, not a deterministic cause or a therapeutic claim, and grounds the appraisal in genetics databases/literature rather than memory.
required_concepts: GBA1 variants are a major genetic risk factor for PD
risk association, not deterministic / fully penetrant
red_flags: classifies as Unsupported or Contradicted despite strong replicated evidence
states GBA1 deterministically causes PD / is fully penetrant
conflates the genetic risk-association claim with a therapeutic claim
relies on memory without grounding in databases/literature

criteria.name: evidence_use
criteria.description: Uses real genetic-association evidence (databases/literature) and cites sources.

criteria.name: preclinical_vs_clinical
criteria.description: Distinguishes a (non-deterministic) risk association from a deterministic cause or therapeutic claim.

criteria.name: uncertainty_handling
criteria.description: Notes penetrance/variant-severity/ancestry nuance without downgrading a well-established association.

criteria.name: avoids_overclaiming
criteria.description: Confident but precise; neither overstates (deterministic cause) nor understates (denies the association).
